ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Non-Asymptotic Sample-Complexity Guarantees for KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Establish non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees for KernelSHAP, proving upper bounds on the number of subset evaluations required to achieve a given accuracy. To do so, analyze the regression formulation of KernelSHAP and use techniques fromΕΠ concentration inequalities to derive a relationship between the sample size, the kernel weights, and the desired precision.
CONTROLS: Analyze the existing implementation of KernelSHAP, compare with existing methods, and compare different sampling distributions (with and without replacement).
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Based on the convergence of KernelSHAP to the exact solution as the sample size increases, the upper bounds will show that a trade-off exists between computational efficiency and estimation accuracy, providing guidance on the optimal choice of sample size. However, a limitation is that these bounds assume independence of the subset evaluations, which may not always be the case in practice.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Unified Framework for Analyzing Randomized Estimators
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework to analyze randomized estimators, including KernelSHAP, unbiased KernelSHAP, and LeverageSHAP, addressing their similarities and differences. This framework will provide a common language to compare and understand the trade-offs between these estimators. Specifically, use techniques from concentration inequalities and convex optimization to derive a general analysis that highlights the impact of the sampling distribution, the regularization parameter, and the precision on the estimator's accuracy.
CONTROLS: Apply the framework to each of the listed estimators, derive explicit bounds, and analyze their relationships.
COST: 2100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The unified framework will reveal that the choice of the sampling distribution and the regularization parameter play critical roles in determining the accuracy of the estimators. However, applying the framework to LeverageSHAP might be challenging due to its dependence on statistical leverage scores.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: LeverageSHAP: Theoretical Analysis and Comparison with KernelSHAP
PROPOSAL: Provide a theoretical analysis of LeverageSHAP, including non-asymptotic sample-complexity guarantees, and compare its performance with KernelSHAP using the unified framework developed in Proposal 2. Derive explicit bounds for LeverageSHAP and analyze its convergence properties. This analysis will help understand the trade-offs between LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP and provide insights into the impact of sampling based on statistical leverage scores.
CONTROLS: Compare LeverageSHAP with KernelSHAP using the unified framework, derive explicit bounds for both methods, and analyze their relationships.
COST: 3700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: LeverageSHAP will be shown to have better sample-complexity guarantees than KernelSHAP, especially for high-dimensional inputs, but may be computationally more expensive due to the calculation of statistical leverage scores. However, the analysis might be challenging due to the dependence of LeverageSHAP on statistical leverage scores.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable Estimation of Shapley Values using Gradient-Based Methods
PROPOSAL: Explore gradient-based methods for estimating Shapley values, such as gradient-based approximation of the Shapley value (GASV) and gradient-based importance sampling (G-IS), to provide scalable alternatives to existing methods. These approaches can potentially leverage the structure of the model and the problem to estimate Shapley values more efficiently. Analyze the convergence properties and sample-complexity guarantees of these methods, comparing them with KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed gradient-based methods with existing methods, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, and analyze the impact of the model's structure and the problem's characteristics on the estimation accuracy.
COST: 4300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The gradient-based methods will demonstrate competitive performance with LeverageSHAP and KernelSHAP, particularly in high-dimensional settings, but may require careful tuning of hyperparameters and may not be suitable for all problem types.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distributed and Parallel Computation of Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Investigate distributed and parallel computation methods for Shapley values, such as using map-reduce or parallel processing libraries, to enable the computation of Shapley values on large-scale datasets. This would make the existing estimators more scalable and applicable to real-world applications. Analyze the communication overhead, synchronization challenges, and potential speedup of parallel computation.
CONTROLS: Implement and compare the parallel computation of existing estimators, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP, on a cluster of GPUs, and analyze the speedup and efficiency of each method.
COST: 14000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The distributed and parallel computation of Shapley values will significantly improve the scalability of existing estimators, but may introduce additional complexity and challenges in implementing and optimizing the parallel computation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Selection Methods for Shapley Values
PROPOSAL: Develop model-selection methods for choosing the most suitable estimator among existing methods, including KernelSHAP, LeverageSHAP, and gradient-based methods, based on the problem characteristics, data distribution, and estimation accuracy. This involves selecting the most relevant features, selecting the optimal sampling distribution, or selecting the best regularization parameter. Analyze the effects of model selection on the estimation accuracy and propose an adaptive model selection method.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of different model selection methods, including cross-validation and conditional mutual information, and analyze their robustness to noise and distribution shift.
COST: 17300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The model selection methods will improve the estimation accuracy and adaptability of existing estimators, but may require careful hyperparameter tuning and may not generalize to all problem types.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Data Distribution on Shapley Value Estimation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of various data distributions, such as non-Gaussian distributions, outliers, and Bauer's uniform distribution, on the estimation accuracy of Shapley values using existing estimators, including KernelSHAP and LeverageSHAP. Analyze the effects of distribution shift on the estimation performance and propose robust estimation methods that can handle different data distributions.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of robust estimation methods, such as robust kernel SHAP and quantile regression SHAP, with the standard estimators, and analyze their robustness to different data distributions.
COST: 21330 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The analysis will reveal that existing estimators are sensitive to distribution shift and outliers, and the proposed robust estimation methods will provide more accurate estimates of Shapley values under various data distributions. However, the robust estimation methods may require careful hyperparameter tuning and may have higher computational cost.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: High-Dimensional Shapley Value Estimation using Sparse Regression
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel method for estimating Shapley values in high-dimensional settings using sparse regression techniques. The proposed method will leverage sparse information about the feature importance to reduce the computational cost of Shapley value estimation. Analyze the effects of using sparse regression on the estimation accuracy and propose an efficient algorithm for high-dimensional sparse regression.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed sparse regression method with existing high-dimensional estimators, such as PathSHAP, and analyze the computational cost of each method.
COST: 26150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The sparse regression method will significantly reduce the computational cost of high-dimensional Shapley value estimation and provide accurate estimates of feature importance, but may require careful hyperparameter tuning and may not generalize to all problem types.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robust Shapley Value Estimation for Outlier-Robust Models
PROPOSAL: Develop robust Shapley value estimation methods for models that are robust to outliers and adversarial attacks. The proposed methods will combine existing Shapley value estimation techniques with robust regression and clustering methods to identify and mitigate the effects of outliers and adversarial attacks. Analyze the effects of using robust regression and clustering on the estimation accuracy and propose efficient algorithms for outlier detection and clustering.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the proposed robust Shapley value estimation methods with existing methods on outlier-ridden and adversarial datasets, and analyze the effects of different robust regression and clustering methods on the estimation accuracy.
COST: 30000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The robust Shapley value estimation methods will provide accurate estimates of feature importance in the presence of outliers and adversarial attacks, but may require careful hyperparameter tuning and may have higher computational cost than existing methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Comparison of Shapley Value Estimation Methods on Real-World Datasets
PROPOSAL: Conduct an extensive experimental comparison of existing and proposed Shapley value estimation methods on various real-world datasets. Analyze the performance of each method in terms of estimation accuracy, computational cost, and robustness to outliers and distribution shift. The ultimate goal is to provide a comprehensive evaluation and comparison of different Shapley value estimation methods, and to identify the strengths and weakness of each approach.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of selected Shapley value estimation methods on a wide range of real-world datasets, including tabular, image, and text datasets.
COST: 50000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experimental comparison will reveal the strengths and weaknesses of different Shapley value estimation methods on real-world datasets, and help practitioners choose the most suitable methods for their specific use cases. However, the extensive experimental comparison will require careful design and implementation of the experiments to ensure unbiased and reliable results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing Long-Range Temporal Dynamics in MLLMs
PROPOSAL: Experiment to evaluate the performance of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in capturing long-range temporal dynamics inthe context of remote sensing change captioning, using a novel temporal understanding protocol. Apply MLLMs to a sequence of temporally ordered satellite images, with a focus on understanding how they comprehend the evolution of changes across long, irregularly sampled sequences. Evaluate MLLMs' performance using a customized version of the COCO Captioning metric, adapted to account for temporal consistency.
CONTROLS: Static image captioning models (e.g., BERT- BASE), as well as baseline MLLMs without temporal attention
COST: 10,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect MLLMs to outperform static image captioning models in capturing temporal relationships, but their performance may struggle with extremely long-range temporal dynamics, where semantic context is lost.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Experiment to evaluate the performance of a novel future satellite image forecasting approach, where visual and textual information from the historical sequence is conditioned on the evolving temporal dynamics. Employ a combination of a diffusion-based image generator and an MLLM trained on a customized temporal change description dataset. Use a variant of the traditionally used Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) metric adapted for temporal consistency in evaluating the forecasts. Test this approach on a proxy dataset (e.g., Sequence-Earth).
CONTROLS: Future satellite image forecasting methods without temporal attention, and forecasts generated by a standard diffusion-based image generator without MLLM guidance
COST: 50,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach is expected to demonstrate significantly improved temporal consistency in generated forecasts compared to standard forecasting methods. However, the model might struggle with capturing the underlying causes of change, leading to realistic but inconsistent forecasts in certain scenarios.

TITLE: A Dataset for Temporal Change Description and Forecasting in Satellite Imagery
PROPOSAL: Create a novel, large-scale dataset (e.g., Satellite Changes in Multifaceted Environments - SCME) for temporal change description and forecasting tasks, featuring images from multiple satellite sources, across diverse geographic locations and scales. Annotate each image with its respective time stamp, location, and a detailed change description. Supplement this dataset with automatically generated textual futures for ground-truth forecasting evaluations
CONTROLS: Existing datasets for satellite image time series analysis (e.g., DIOR, Sequence-Earth)
COST: 171,909 GPU-hours (estimating 35 days of actual compute time with 1.2K GPU nodes)
PREDICTION: This dataset is expected to serve as a comprehensive benchmark for future research in the domain, with its large scale and rich annotations facilitating the development and evaluation of more effective models for temporal change description and forecasting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Forecasted Images
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel metric, TCSS (Temporal Consistency Score for Satellite Series), to measure the temporal consistency of forecasted images in the context of satellite image time series forecasting. TCSS assesses the consistency of forecasted images with the observed historical trends and dynamics using a combination of spatial and temporal features derived from the image sequence
CONTROLS: Traditional image-quality metrics (e.g., SSIM, PSNR), as well as existing metrics for temporal consistency in video forecasts (e.g., MTDC, TGVC)
COST: 2,160 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: TCSS is expected to effectively capture the temporal consistency in forecasted images, providing a more comprehensive evaluation of forecasting models than existing metrics. However, the model might struggle with accurately capturing complex changes in the historical sequence, leading to false negatives in certain cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Attention in MLLMs for Remote Sensing Change Captioning
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel MLLM architecture, HSA-MLLM (Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Attention Multimodal Large Language Model), featuring a hierarchical spatiotemporal attention mechanism to improve the model's understanding of long-range temporal dynamics and semantic evolution in remote sensing change captioning
CONTROLS: Standard MLLM architectures (e.g., BERT, ROUTE), as well as the original MLLM in Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting
COST: 105,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: HSA-MLLM is expected to significantly outperform standard MLLMs in capturing long-range temporal dynamics and semantic evolution, leading to more accurate change descriptions in remote sensing change captioning. However, the model's computational complexity might become a limiting factor for very long sequences.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE:  Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Attention in MLLMs for Remote Sensing Change Captioning
PROPOSAL: Revise HSA-MLLM to incorporate a novel graph-based approach, called Temporal Graph Attention (TGA), to model the complex relationships between images in the sequence and capture the underlying causal narrative of changes. TGA constructs a temporal graph from the input sequence, where nodes represent images and edges represent the spatial and temporal relationships between them
CONTROLS: The revised HSA-MLLM without TGA, as well as the original MLLM architectures
COST: 175,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised HSA-MLLM with TGA is expected to significantly improve the model's understanding of the underlying causal narrative of changes, leading to more accurate and temporally consistent change descriptions in remote sensing change captioning. However, the model's performance might suffer from overfitting if the graph structure is not well-regularized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Impact of Irregularly Sampled Sequences on Remote Sensing Change Captioning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of irregularly sampled sequences on remote sensing change captioning tasks using a controlled experiment. Evaluate how different sequence sampling strategies (e.g., uniform, non-uniform, and synthetic) impact the performance of MLLMs, including the revised HSA-MLLM with TGA. Assess the robustness of these models to the gap size between consecutive images, as well as their ability to generalize to unseen sequences with the same characteristics
CONTROLS: Experiments using uniformly sampled sequences, as well as standard MLLM architectures
COST: 60,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The study is expected to provide valuable insights into the impact of sequence sampling strategies on remote sensing change captioning tasks and highlight the strengths and limitations of MLLMs in handling irregularly sampled sequences.

TITLE: Neural Temporal Transformer for Satellite Image Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel neural network architecture, Neural Temporal Transformer (NTT), featuring a hierarchical transformer encoder-decoder structure to model the temporal dependencies in satellite image time series forecasting. NTT is designed to capture the complex patterns and(long-term dependencies in the data, while allowing for efficient and parallelizable computing
CONTROLS: Standard transformer-based architectures for time series forecasting, as well as the approach in Temporally Consistent Future Satellite Image Forecasting
COST: 216,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: NTT is expected to significantly improve the accuracy of satellite image time series forecasting tasks, particularly for long-term horizons and complex sequences. However, the model's computational complexity might become a limiting factor for very long sequences.

TITLE: A Calibrated Approach to Evaluating Temporal Consistency in Satellite Image Forecasting
PROPOSAL: Introduce a probabilistic framework for evaluating the temporal consistency of satellite image forecasts, incorporating uncertainty quantification and model calibration. Develop a novel calibration metric, Calibration-Score for Temporal Consistency (CSTC), to measure the agreement between the model's predicted uncertainty and the observed temporal consistency in the data
CONTROLS: Traditional metrics for temporal consistency, as well as existing approaches to uncertainty quantification and model calibration
COST: 300,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The probabilistic framework and CSTC metric are expected to improve the evaluation of temporal consistency in satellite image forecasts, providing a more accurate and reliable assessment of model performance. However, the approach might require significant computational resources for large-scale evaluations.

ACTION: REVISE 3

PROPOSAL: Revise the SCME dataset to include an additional annotation task, where human annotators provide uncertainty scores for the predicted changes, which can be used to evaluate the model's uncertainty quantification
CONTROLS: The original SCME dataset, as well as existing approaches for uncertainty quantification in remote sensing change captioning
COST: 500,000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised SCME dataset with uncertainty scores is expected to provide a more comprehensive evaluation of model performance, particularly for tasks that involve uncertainty quantification. This will enable deeper insights into the strengths and limitations of remote sensing change captioning models and promote the development of more robust and reliable models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Updating Different Model Components on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will conduct an experiment where we update different components of a pre-trained forecasting model during online deployment to identify which parts of the model are most sensitive to distribution shift and concept drift in real-world traffic flow forecasting data. We will compare the performance of updating (1) the final prediction layer, (2) the ensemble weights, (3) the adapter module, and (4) the full model weights.
CONTROLS: We will use the same model architecture, optimizer, and hyperparameters for all updates, and compare against a baseline where the model weights are frozen during deployment.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: We expect to see that updating the adapter module or the final prediction layer performs better than freezing the model weights, but the ensemble weights might not be as effective. The full model weights might be difficult to update online due to high variance of gradient estimates. We hypothesize that the performance of the baseline (frozen model weights) will be inferior to all other update strategies, and may fail in scenarios with rapid distribution shift or concept drift.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Performance of Experience Replay in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will implement and compare two experience replay strategies in online time series forecasting: (1) epistemic replay, which reuses observed samples and adds them to an experience replay buffer to stabilize model updates, and (2) temporal replay, which selects samples from the buffer based on their temporal proximity to the current observation to encourage the model to learn from past observations relevant to the current distribution.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of both experience replay strategies against an oracle baseline that has access to the entire training dataset at each time step.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: We expect to see that temporal replay outperforms epistemic replay in scenarios with rapid concept drift, as it enables the model to learn from observations that are more relevant to the current distribution. However, epistemic replay might be more effective in scenarios with few observations and high variance of gradient estimates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparing the Robustness of Gradient-Based Updates and Model-Based Updates in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will compare the performance of online gradient descent (OGD) updates against model-based updates, which use a small batch of recent samples to directly fit the parameters of a linear adapter on top of the pre-trained model. We will compare the robustness of both update strategies in scenarios with distribution shift and concept drift.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline that uses OGD updates.
COST: 7000
PREDICTION: We expect to see that model-based updates are more robust to distribution shift and concept drift than gradient-based updates (OGD), as they do not rely on gradient estimates from few samples. However, OGD updates might be more effective in scenarios with few observations and high variance of gradient estimates.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Comparing the Robustness of Gradient-Based Updates and Model-Based Updates in Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will modify the proposal to include a filtering step when updating the adapter's parameters in the model-based update strategy, which will select the most relevant features for the adapter based on the gradients computed from the recent samples. We expect this filtered version of model-based updates to achieve a better balance between robustness and adaptability.
CONTROLS: We will continue to compare against a baseline that uses online gradient descent (OGD) updates.
COST: 7000 (no change)
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the filtered model-based updates achieve a better balance between robustness and adaptability than the unfiltered model-based updates, and outperform OGD updates in scenarios with distribution shift and concept drift. However, OGD updates might still be more effective in scenarios with few observations and high variance of gradient estimates.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Attention for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will design a temporal attention mechanism that selectively focuses on recent samples when updating the model's parameters, and weight them based on their relevance to the current distribution. We will integrate the temporal attention mechanism with both OGD updates and model-based updates to improve their robustness to distribution shift and concept drift.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of temporal attention-integrated updates against the baseline OGD updates and model-based updates.
COST: 10680
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the temporal attention-integrated updates significantly improve the robustness and adaptability of both OGD updates and model-based updates, especially in scenarios with rapid concept drift. However, adding the extra attention computation might increase the latency of the model updates.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Updating Different Model Components on Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will modify the proposal to include additional experimental results for two more traffic flow forecasting datasets: M5 and SNAP. We will also explore the effect of different adapter module architectures on the update performance, such as simple multilayer perceptrons versus convolutional neural networks.
CONTROLS: The comparison will remain with the same baseline (freezing the model weights) and update strategies (final prediction layer, ensemble weights, and full model weights).
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the results hold across multiple traffic flow forecasting datasets and that the performance of different adapter module architectures yields different improvements in update performance. However, the results might be less consistent across different datasets, and the impact of the adapter module architecture might be data-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Delayed Feedback Compensation for Multi-Step Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate a delay compensation mechanism to alleviate the issues arising from delayed feedback in multi-step forecasting. The mechanism uses a ensemble of models, each trained to forecast a different step-ahead horizon, and calculates a weighted average of their predictions to obtain the final forecast. We will explore the use of different weighting schemes to improve the performance of the mechanism.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of the delay compensation mechanism against the baseline OGD updates and model-based updates, as well as our previously proposed temporal attention-integrated updates.
COST: 15360
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the delay compensation mechanism effectively improves the forecasting performance of multi-step forecasting tasks, and that the weighted average of model predictions is a good approach to compensating for delayed feedback. However, the performance might degrade when the number of steps ahead increases, and the optimal weighting scheme might be highly problem-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Whittle's Index-based Model Selection for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop and evaluate an online model selection mechanism based on Whittle's index, which determines when to update the model and which parameters to update by computing a score that reflects the expected reduction in cumulative regret. We will compare the performance of the Whittle's index-based model selection mechanism against the baseline update strategies and our previously proposed update mechanisms.
CONTROLS: We will compare against the OGD updates, model-based updates, temporal attention-integrated updates, and delay compensation mechanism.
COST: 21600
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the Whittle's index-based model selection mechanism effectively balances exploration and exploitation, and outperforms the baseline update strategies and previously proposed update mechanisms in scenarios with concept drift and distribution shift. However, the performance might degrade when the number of parameters to update increases, and the effective computation of Whittle's index might be challenging in high-dimensional spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theory of Dynamic Regret for Online Time Series Forecasting with Non-Stationary Distributions
PROPOSAL: We will develop a theoretical framework for analyzing the dynamic regret of online time series forecasting algorithms with non-stationary distributions. We will derive bounds on the dynamic regret in terms of the cumulative variation of the optimal parameters over time and the variance of gradient estimates, and explore the implications for the design of online update strategies.
CONTROLS: We will assume access to the underlying data-generating process and will not consider sublinear constraints on the number of passes through the data.
COST: 32400
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the theoretical framework provides insight into the trade-offs between exploration and exploitation in online time series forecasting and that the bounds on the dynamic regret can guide the design of more effective update strategies. However, the theoretical analysis might be limited to special cases or abstract scenarios, and the results might not directly translate to online learning with complex, real-world data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Domain-Adversarial Training Method for Online Time Series Forecasting
PROPOSAL: We will develop a domain-adversarial training method for online time series forecasting by augmenting the forecasting model with an auxiliary discriminator that distinguishes between the online and offline data distributions. The discriminator is trained simultaneously with the forecasting model to adapt the model to changing data distributions and improve its robustness to out-of-distribution data.
CONTROLS: We will compare the performance of our proposed domain-adversarial training method against the baseline update strategies, update mechanisms, and theoretical analysis.
COST: 37020
PREDICTION: We expect to see that the domain-adversarial training method improves the robustness and adaptability of online time series forecasting models, and that the auxiliary discriminator effectively captures the differences between online and offline data distributions. However, the method might be computationally expensive and difficult to tune, and the performance improvements might be problem-dependent.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Heterogeneous Multimodal Encoder Aggregation for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method for combining the outputs of heterogeneous multimodal encoders, specifically designed for visual document retrieval. Our approach, called Heterogeneous Multimodal Encoder Embeddings (HME2), employs a lightweight neural network to learn sub-space alignments between the representations of two different encoders. The idea is to project the high-dimensional embedding of each encoder into a lower-dimensional space that is common to both, allowing us to leverage the complementary strengths of each retriever. HME2 integrates smoothly with the late-interaction approach of ColPali-based encoders, requiring no modifications to the existing architecture.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla ColPali-based encoder; Baseline 2: dense text retriever alone; Baseline 3: hybrid retrieval at rank/score level.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: HME2 significantly improves the trade-off between retrieval quality and online latency/index memory, compared to scaling up the representations of a single model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Visual Document Retrieval via Knowledge Distillation from Heterogeneous Multimodal Encoders
PROPOSAL: To further enhance the complementary signals of heterogeneous multimodal encoders, we propose a knowledge distillation framework, called KD-HME2. KD-HME2 leverages the teacher-student paradigm, where the output of the HME2 framework is used as a soft label to train a smaller, more compact multimodal encoder. The goal is to learn a more lite-weight representation of the visual document, which can be more efficient and scalable. We explore different distillation methods, including cross-entropy loss and trip-force margin-based loss.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla ColPali-based encoder; Baseline 2: HME2; Baseline 3: KD-HME2 without HME2 framework.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: KD-HME2 improves both the retrieval quality and the model flexibility/layout/overall accuracy tradeoffs. However, quantization might be hard on ColPali as those CNN models generally do not quantize well to bitwidths below 8.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: An Empirical Study of Heterogeneous Multimodal Encoder Aggregations for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: We conduct an in-depth empirical analysis of different aggregation strategies within the HME2 framework. Specifically, we investigate 1) vector concatenation, 2) attention-based fusion, 3) neural network-based fusion, and 4) diagonal basis intersection. The goal is to understand which aggregation strategy is most suitable for visual document retrieval and why. We also explore the impact of different evaluation metrics, including recall@k, precision@k, and mean averages precision (MAP).
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla ColPali-based encoder; Baseline 2: HME2 with different aggregation strategies.
COST: 6701
PREDICTION: Empirical experiments reveal that attention-based fusion and neural network-based fusion outperform vector concatenation and diagonal basis intersection. Hyperparameter tuning of dense and attentional components does have impact on the performances of corresponding aggregator approaches, where multiple bandwidths turned are the best solution across all found possibilities.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Modality Gap in Visual Document Retrieval: A Transfer Learning Approach
PROPOSAL: We investigate the modality gap in visual document retrieval, where the substantial difference between text and images may hinder the performance of vision-centric models. Our approach, called TransferHME2, employs transfer learning to adapt the HME2 framework pre-trained on a large-scale text corpus to a specific visual document retrieval task. We evaluate the effectiveness of TransferHME2 on multiple benchmarks, including PubMed and arXiv, and compare its performance with other transfer learning approaches, such as fine-tuning the entire model from scratch.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla ColPali-based encoder; Baseline 2: HME2; Baseline 3: TransferHME2; Baseline 4: fine-tuning the entire model from scratch.
COST: 8340
PREDICTION: TransferHME2 reduces the modality gap between text and images, achieving state-of-the-art results on multiple visual document retrieval benchmarks. However, the performance of TransferHME2 may suffer when the target task differs significantly from the pre-training corpus.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient and Scalable Visual Document Retrieval via Hierarchical Neural Indexing
PROPOSAL: To further improve the scalability and efficiency of the visual document retrieval system, we propose a hierarchical neural indexing approach, called HIN-HME2. HIN-HME2 organizes the document embeddings in a hierarchical manner, using a neural network to learn the intermediate representations and cluster the embeddings. This allows for efficient and scalable approximate nearest neighbor search using a custom-designed indexing data structure. We evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of HIN-HME2 on multiple benchmarks and show that it significantly reduces the latency and memory overhead of the system.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla ColPali-based encoder; Baseline 2: HME2; Baseline 3: HIN-HME2; Baseline 4: HIN-HME2 with different indexing methods.
COST: 10200
PREDICTION: HIN-HME2 achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple visual document retrieval benchmarks, with significant improvements in latency and memory efficiency. However, the performance of HIN-HME2 may suffer when the hierarchical indexing structure becomes too complex or unwieldy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Granularity Kernel-Based Similarity Measures for Visual Document Retrieval
PROPOSAL: To address the challenges of measuring similarity between complex visual documents and queries, we propose a kernel-based approach, called MK-HME2, which combines multiple granularity kernel-based similarity measures. MK-HME2 leverages the strengths of different kernels, including the Bag-of-Words (BoW) kernel and the Fisher Vectors (FV) kernel, to capture various aspects of visual document structure and content. We evaluate the effectiveness of MK-HME2 on multiple benchmarks and show that it outperforms previous state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: vanilla ColPali-based encoder; Baseline 2: HME2; Baseline 3: MK-HME2; Baseline 4: MK-HME2 with different kernel combinations.
COST: 12600
PREDICTION: MK-HME2 achieves state-of-the-art results on multiple visual document retrieval benchmarks, with improvements in both precision and recall. However, the performance of MK-HME2 may suffer when the kernel combinations become too complex or computationally expensive.

ACTION: ADD
